title: Review shareholder–corporation transactions — Alder Corp. and Nina Vance
instructions: Nina Vance is the sole shareholder and CEO of Alder Corp., a C corporation with ample E&P. A staff member prepared the 2025 amounts for Alder's Form 1120 and Nina's Form 1040 from the documents below. Review them, then resolve the review notes. Tick every amount that is wrong and enter the correct amount.

exhibits.title: Documents (2025)
exhibits.content:
- **Loan agreement:** on January 1, Alder lent Nina **$200,000**, interest-free and payable on demand. The loan was outstanding all year. Nina used the money to renovate her home. The blended annual rate for 2025 (given): **4%**.
- **Lease:** Alder rents its office building from Nina for **$120,000** a year. An independent appraisal puts fair rental value at **$80,000**.
- **Compensation:** Alder paid Nina a salary of **$300,000**. An independent compensation study found **$250,000** reasonable for her duties.
- Alder's current and accumulated E&P exceed **$1 million**.

rows.label: Alder — interest income on the shareholder loan
rows.explanation: An interest-free **demand** loan from a corporation to its shareholder is a below-market loan (§7872). Foregone interest, 200,000 × 4% = **8,000**, is interest income to Alder.

rows.label: Alder — rent expense deducted
rows.explanation: Only fair rental value, **80,000**, is an ordinary and necessary expense. The 40,000 excess is a constructive dividend.

rows.label: Alder — compensation deducted for Nina
rows.explanation: Only **reasonable** compensation (250,000 per the independent study) is deductible (§162(a)(1)). The 50,000 excess is a constructive dividend.

rows.label: Alder — deduction for constructive dividends
rows.explanation: Dividends are never deductible by a C corporation. **No error.**

rows.label: Nina — dividend income
rows.explanation: Deemed dividend on the loan 8,000 + excess rent 40,000 + excess compensation 50,000 = **98,000**, all within E&P.

rows.label: Nina — wages
rows.explanation: **250,000**; the excess is reclassified as a dividend.

rows.label: Nina — deductible interest on the shareholder loan
rows.explanation: Nina used the money personally, so the deemed interest is nondeductible personal interest: **0**.

rows.label: A separate 2022 advance of $75,000 to Nina: no note, no interest, no repayments, no collateral, and Nina says she does not intend to repay.
options: Treat it as a bona fide loan
Treat it as a constructive dividend when made
rows.answer: Treat it as a constructive dividend when made
rows.explanation: Without the substance of a debt (a note, interest, repayment, intent to repay), the advance is a distribution.

rows.label: The $200,000 loan is below the de minimis amount for below-market loans.
options: Incorrect — the $10,000 de minimis exception does not apply
rows.answer: Incorrect — the $10,000 de minimis exception does not apply
rows.explanation: The corporation–shareholder de minimis exception covers loans of 10,000 or less.
